server/src/logging/logging.module.spec.ts is not part of this feature's plan. The change is test-only: it raises that file's Jest timeout to 120s because its beforeAll boots the whole AppModule and waits for the pino transport (~50s alone, more under load), so the 30s project default killed the hook. Accepted as a load accommodation, not production behaviour; no application code changed.

The red run that motivated the fix (12:38Z evidence) failed 23 tests across FOUR suites and missed the global coverage thresholds (statements 78.41%, lines 77.39%) as a consequence of those suites not running. The commit message and the in-file comment attribute the failure to the logging suite alone, which the evidence does not support. The subsequent green run shows the cause was machine load rather than one suite, but the record understates it.

The test report cited .sdrive/reports/tests/raw/shared-package-v1-2026-11-04.log as the raw log for the 92-test measurement, but that file contains the earlier 63-test run. Corrected in the report during this review; the governed evidence JSON is the authoritative record for the later runs.

Two backoffice tests outside this feature (register-wizard.test.tsx, accept-invite.test.tsx) still use Vitest's 5s default and can time out when the machine is CPU-saturated. Only the first has an explicit budget. Pre-existing and out of this feature's scope, but it is the same class of load sensitivity that produced the red runs.
eslint over backoffice/test/ reports a pre-existing unused `tmpdir` import; the project's lint script only covers src, so it is not part of any configured check.
server/package.json keeps a dead test:e2e script pointing at a non-existent ./test/jest-e2e.json (CON-409 known defect).
Self-review disclosed and owner-accepted (C18). Kept in the record so the verdict does not rest on an independent party.

security.reason: No secrets in the diff; no new production dependency (only the @riaya/shared workspace link). The package is schemas and types only and touches no authentication, user input or HTTP surface, so the CON-51x baseline controls are not applicable rather than unverified. CI's gitleaks secret scan passed on this commit.

baseline.detail: The package authenticates nothing and issues no tokens.
No routes, guards or role checks exist in packages/shared.
No HTTP server is created by the package.
The package defines schemas consumed by existing DTOs; it adds no request boundary of its own.
No data access, no ORM, no SQL.
No rendering surface; no React or HTML output.
No cookies, sessions or state-changing routes.
The package reads no environment variable (NFR-004), verified by AC-005's boundary test.

performance.reason: The specification declares no performance, accessibility or SEO NFR. NFR-001..NFR-005 are structural constraints and are each bound to a tested AC, so there is no target to measure.
